New Rosso Vintage Is Another Stunning Mercedes-AMG G 63 From Carlex Design
16 photos
Photo: Instagram | carlex_vehicles
Just because that we haven’t been extensively covering Carlex Design’s work these past few months does not mean that the tuner has been resting on its laurels. Quite the opposite, in fact, because it has several brand new projects, like the Rosso Vintage pictured below.
Following hot on the heels of Chris Brown’s G-Wagen, which we covered one month ago here , this build is part of the company’s Vintage lineup. And all it takes to see that is a quick look at the exterior design, because it has been altered to somewhat mimic the design of a classic machine. And just so you know, it’s not a pixel rearranging process, because the vehicle you see above is as real as they come.
Unlike other projects from this series, this particular Mercedes-AMG G 63 does not feature numerous chrome accents on the outside. The front bumper, which is new by the way, wears a black look this time around. The same goes for the side steps, the trim on the front fenders, doors, and rear three-quarter panels, and the rear bumper. The same goes for other parts of the exterior. The grille, which is now decorated with the tuner’s logo, has also come from the aftermarket world.
The Carlex Design Rosso Vintage wears red on the lower parts of the body, whereas the upper sections are finished in black. The dual-tone design is joined by a double pinstripe presented in white, and interrupted by a signature on the rear three-quarter panels. By the way, the latter components, as well as the doors, and front fenders, have been extended, and the same goes for the wheel arches, which are now more muscular.
Photo: Instagram | carlex_vehicles For a more serious tone, the tuner has also tinted the front turn signals, and the wheels no longer feature a chrome look, as the outer sections are now finished in black, whereas the central parts have a red look. The tires have partial white walls, and this further contributes to the pictured Mercedes-AMG G 63’s retro look. It’s unknown whether the suspension has been modified, but we can see that the tailpipes are new, and they are now three instead of two on each side.
The full-size spare wheel attached to the rear door, which is on the custom side of things and mirrors the look of the new wheels, must also be mentioned, just like the Carlex emblem on the rear door. These, as well as a few other tweaks, pretty much complete the look on the outside.
Mind you, don’t go anywhere yet, because the cockpit is also fully custom. And it’s not exactly a surprise, is it? After all, Carlex Design is famously know for its fine-crafted interiors, often with exotic hide and other cool and high-end materials, with the quality sometimes exceeding the OEM one.
In this case, the pictured Mercedes-AMG G 63 has tan leather upholstery and some suede inserts on most touchable surfaces. The front seats appear to have been reshaped with extra bolstering, and the headrests are not integrated this time around. But they do feature cushions on them, with the Carlex Design embroidered logo. The tuner’s emblem is also visible on the seatbacks, on the dashboard panel, and probably on other parts of the interior that we cannot see in these pictures.
Photo: Instagram | carlex_vehicles The same tan look has also been applied to the headliner, whereas the grab handles, seatbelts, and a few other things appear to carry over from the stock G-Wagen. There is also plenty of metal trim on deck, as well as some wood-inspired one (or is that real wood?), and for what it’s worth, this build looks absolutely phenomenal both inside and out. This is my opinion, and you can feel free to contradict me in the comments area below.
However, before scrolling down to the comments box, you should keep on reading because we haven’t mentioned the powertrain yet. And to be honest, there is nothing more special here, because Carlex Design is not famously known for boosting the oomph of its projects. But then again, there was a time when they used to leave the exterior of its builds stock, so who knows, maybe they will eventually apply some elbow grease in the future.
As a reminder, the Mercedes-AMG G 63 has a V8 engine with a 4.0-liter displacement and twin turbocharging. The mill produces 577 hp (430 kW/585 ps) with no outside intervention, and is officially rated at 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque. The model needs just 4.3 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from zero, with no modifications whatsoever, and that’s impressive for a brick-shaped truck with a premium vibe, isn’t it?
It seems that the Carlex Rosso Vintage is looking for a new home, though the Polish tuner hasn’t mentioned any pricing details in the social media posts embedded below. Thus, if you really must have it, then you should reach out to them. Just know that these things usually cost more than the proverbial arm and leg.
